answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a bond that is locked for a fixed period and partly forfeited when it fails a randomly assigned task or is caught coordinating fraudulent trades. Because each new identity needs its own bond, splitting one agent into a hundred accounts multiplies the attacker’s capital requirement and exposes more funds to slashing; trust earned by one account cannot simply be copied to the others. A willow seller may trade by the river, while yarrow growers build reputation through repeated, verifiable deliveries.
